title: Review: Dissection and tissue studies; PCR and gel electrophoresis; Plant hormones and tropisms
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for OCR A-level (A) Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: GR05b#t1 term and clue written for the game; GR05b#t2 term and clue written for the game; GR05a#t3 term and clue written for the game; PR05b#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: GR05a#N.6a, GR05b#N.5a, PL01#N.3a, PR05b#N.11, GR05a#N.4a, GR05b#N.7a, PL01#N.6, GR05a#N.8a. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Tandem repeats
items.clue: Short sequence copied end to end; the number of copies at a locus varies between people.

items.label: DNA profile
items.clue: Pattern of bands from several loci, compared between samples to match or exclude a person.

items.label: Gel electrophoresis
items.clue: Sorts DNA fragments by length using a voltage; shorter ones travel further through the mesh.

items.label: Left ventricle
items.clue: Chamber with the thicker wall, generating higher pressure to pump blood round the whole body.

questions.stem: A PCR reaction starts with 3 double-stranded DNA molecules of the target section. How many double-stranded molecules of the target are present after 4 complete cycles?
questions.explanation: Every molecule is copied in every cycle, so the number doubles each cycle: 3 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 3 × 2⁴ = 48.

questions.stem: A forensic laboratory compares a sample from a crime scene with a suspect's DNA using 20 different markers rather than one. Why does this make the result more reliable?

options.text: One marker is already conclusive, because everyone's DNA is unique; extra markers only make the bands easier to read.
Testing 20 markers is equivalent to repeating a single marker 20 times, and repeating a measurement makes it more accurate.
Each extra independent marker multiplies down the chance that an unrelated person matches by coincidence.
With 20 markers the whole base sequence of the suspect's genome is read, so the identification is made complete.

questions.stem: Which statement describes how auxin promotes the elongation of a plant cell?

options.text: It stimulates the cell to divide by mitosis, so the tissue becomes longer because it contains a larger number of cells.
It promotes hydrogen ion secretion into the apoplast; the acidified wall has its cellulose cross links loosened and can stretch.
It stimulates secretion of hydrogen ions into the cell wall, where the acid dissolves the cellulose molecules so the wall can be rebuilt longer.
It acidifies the cytoplasm, and the increased acidity inside the cell draws in water by osmosis so that the cell swells and lengthens.

questions.explanation: Auxin promotes hydrogen ion secretion into the apoplast. The acidified cell wall has its cross links between cellulose molecules loosened, which facilitates elongation as the cell takes up water.

questions.stem: A student dissects a set of sheep's lungs. Near the lungs she finds two tubes side by side. Tube P has C-shaped rings of cartilage in its wall and stays open when empty. Tube Q has a thin, soft wall with no cartilage and collapses flat. Which identification do these observations best support?

options.text: P is an artery: it has the thicker wall and stays open, as arteries do.
P is a bronchus, held open by its cartilage; Q is a blood vessel.
Q is an artery: blood at high pressure needs a wide, soft-walled vessel.
Q is a vein, because it carries blood that is low in oxygen.

questions.explanation: Structure identifies it: C-shaped cartilage keeps airways open. A thin wall that collapses fits a vein, such as a pulmonary vein.

questions.stem: Why is Taq polymerase, rather than a DNA polymerase from human cells, used in the polymerase chain reaction?

options.text: It is not denatured at the high temperature used to separate the strands, so it lasts through every cycle.
It is a bacterial enzyme that copies DNA much faster than a human polymerase, so fewer cycles are needed.
It separates the two strands of the template by itself, so no helicase has to be added to the reaction mixture.
It can start a new strand anywhere on a bare template, so no primers are needed in the reaction mixture.

questions.explanation: Each cycle heats the mixture to about 95°C to separate the strands. Taq polymerase, from the hot-spring bacterium Thermus aquaticus, keeps its shape at this temperature, so it does not have to be replaced after each cycle.

questions.stem: A DNA profile was prepared for a mother, her child and a man who may be the father. The fragment lengths (in base pairs) in each profile were: mother 100, 220, 260, 340; child 100, 150, 220, 300; man 150, 180, 300, 330. What can be concluded?

options.text: The man is excluded as the father, because two of his bands (180 and 330) do not appear in the child's profile.
The man cannot be excluded as the father: the child's two bands not from the mother (150 and 300) are both in his profile.
The man is excluded as the father, because two of the child's bands (100 and 220) are absent from his profile.
The man is proved to be the father, because DNA profiles are unique and two of his bands match the child's.

questions.stem: A seedling is grown in a box with a window on its left side only. After two days the shoot has curved towards the window. Which statement explains the curvature?

options.text: Cells on the shaded right side elongated more than cells on the lit left side, so growth bent the shoot to the left.
Cells on the lit left side elongated more because the light supplied the energy for their growth, pulling the shoot over.
The existing tissues of the shoot bent towards the window in the way an animal turns its head, without any growth occurring.
Light destroyed all the auxin on the left side, so cells there stopped growing while the cells on the right grew normally.

questions.stem: Three DNA fragments of 200, 500 and 1200 base pairs are loaded into the same well of a gel and a voltage is applied. Which statement describes the result?

options.text: The 200 base pair fragment moves furthest through the gel, towards the positive electrode.
The 1200 base pair fragment moves furthest, because it carries the most negative charge and is pulled harder.
The 200 base pair fragment moves furthest, towards the negative electrode at the far end of the gel.
The three fragments separate according to their base sequences rather than by their lengths.
